titleStmt.title: Telegram From Secretary of State Shultz’s Delegation to the White House and the Department of State

div.head: 475. Telegram From Secretary of State Shultz’s Delegation to the White House and the Department of State
div.p: Secto 2035. Subject: Memorandum for the President: Meeting with President Lusinchi, Feb 3.
3. President Lusinchi was visibly moved by your letter of congratulations and accepted in principle our invitation to make a State visit May 15.

4. Lusinchi is a veteran politician with good instincts. But he faces massive problems and is not fully informed on their wider implications. We need to move quickly to consolidate our ties, and I am arranging an interagency follow-on to brief him on Central America.
5. Three themes dominated my private meeting with him. They were Venezuela’s economic difficulties, Central America, and how to strengthen our cooperation on both.

6. Lusinchi wants to play a role on Central America. He is convinced that Cuba is an enemy of Venezuela quite as much as of the United States, and wants to be supportive on Grenada. But his information on Nicaragua and El Salvador comes more from the political left than his own military and intelligence communities. We agreed that our Ambassador George Landau would coordinate a continuing exchange of information beginning with a visit to Caracas by a combined State-Defense intelligence team. Details for Cap’s, [less than one line not declassified] and Bud’s consideration will follow separately.

7. Lusinchi brought up Venezuela’s economic troubles persistently. He knows that he has a lot to do himself, but is eager for our help in debt rescheduling and with the banks. He also specifically mentioned EXIM, CCC credits, and the high cost of the F16 fleet they bought from us. I told him we wanted to be constructive, the bankers were aware of Venezuela’s problems but our influence over them was limited. I added that Venezuela could improve the climate by settling the problem of oil compensation. Lusinchi agreed and may take action on this long-lingering issue.

8. While we are not in a position to offer much concrete assistance to Venezuela, I offered to arrange consultations over the full range of Venezuela’s economic problems. I will talk to Don Regan and others about this when I return to Washington. Venezuela’s economic problems are so deep they will
require very careful management to prevent social unrest and a negative impact on our relations. Both State and Treasury will have to sharpen their focus on these issues. At the same time, as in the case of Argentina, its resource base is such that sound management can bring stability and growth in a reasonable time.

note.p: Source: Reagan Library, Executive Secretariat, NSC Country File, Latin America/Central, Venezuela (02/03/1984–12/17/1984). Secret; Immediate; Nodis. Printed from a copy that indicates the original was received in the White House Situation Room. Shultz travelled to Brazil February 3–7, 1984. See Documents 181 and 182.

Reagan’s letter of congratulations to Lusinchi has not been found. In telegram Secto 2049 from Secretary of State Shultz’s Delegation in Brasilia, February 6, the Delegation sent a memorandum of Shultz’s February 3 private meeting with Lusinchi, Landau, and Morales Paúl. (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, N840003–0011) In telegram 1050 from Caracas, February 3, the Embassy reported on Shultz’s February 3 working breakfast with Lusinchi and other U.S. and Venezuelan officials. (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D840075–0370)

In telegram Secto 2036 from Secretary of State Shultz’s Delegation in Rio de Janeiro, February 4, Shultz informed McFarlane, Weinberger, and [name not declassified] that he had “agreed February 3 with President Lusinchi that we would provide him continuing in-depth political/military intelligence on Central America. It is obvious to us that he is getting poor information. We should strike while the iron is hot.” Shultz then outlined a briefing plan. (Reagan Library, Executive Secretariat, NSC Country File, Latin America/Central, Venezuela (02/03/1984–12/17/1984))
